thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Elevated 5xx + latency observed in us-east-1 affecting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. 5xx spike started ~3167777700, rate ~12% for tokens, latency p95 > 1200ms. Possible downstream auth/observability dependency failures. Metrics: https://metrics.redwood/alerts/3167777777

maria: I'm oncall, looking at auth (STS) and CW ingestion errors. Seeing a ton of STS 5xx/504s from the region and CloudWatch Logs ingestion 429s.

ashwin: Runtime-side traces show large number of model request failures when retrieving credentials for customer-managed S3/KMS flows. Also KV cache miss storm for some long-lived chats.

jon: Quick checks: are we hitting upstream STS throttles or an ALB/NLB issue? Any network egress errors?

maria: From VPC NAT logs: increased egress retries to sts.amazonaws.com in us-east-1, many TCP RSTs. AWS status page shows "partial regional degradation" in us-east-1 for STS and CloudWatch in progress.

kevin: Dedicated pools in us-east-1 are showing elevated request errors, but some pools in us-west-2 are healthy. We should fail traffic at the routing layer to prefer us-west-2 for new requests. Existing long-lived sessions should be sticky.

ashwin: Plan suggestion: 1) set routing policy to prefer us-west-2 for control-plane and generation requests; 2) bump token cache TTLs to avoid STS calls; 3) throttle/queue noisy tenants to protect overall latency.

maria: I'll execute routing change. Tagging @pagerduty-bot for handoff.

maria: Executing temporary routing preference now:

```
# control-plane API
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"policy":"prefer-region","region":"us-west-2","scope":"hosted,dedicated","ttl_seconds":600}'
```

maria: API accepted, policy rollout started. Confirming downstream proxies are receiving new routing rules.

jon: I'll start reconfiguring load-balancer fallback for dedicated pools: will drain us-east-1 standby nodes for new sessions.

kevin: Doing drain now on dedicated-pool-eus1-*. Command: `poolctl drain --pool=dedicated-eus1 --mode=graceful --max-conn=0`

kevin: Drain in progress, existing requests will finish, new capacity should route to us-west-2.

ashwin: Enabling model-variant fallback for hosting runtime (so if a shard fails due to credential errors we'll fall back to a compatible variant in another region).

```
# runtime flag
POST /runtime/config
{"model_variant_fallback":true, "fallback_strategy":"region_aware"}
```

maria: Also increasing STS token cache TTLs to reduce calls: updating service config.

```
# example config change
PATCH /services/auth-cache
{"default_ttl_seconds":3600, "max_ttl_seconds":7200}
```

maria: Token TTL pushed. Expect fewer STS calls in ~30s (existing tokens remain until expiry).

tara: CS update: notifying top 20 enterprise accounts with possible elevated errors and mitigation steps. Draft message in #customer-notifications, will push if we hit 15% error or breach SLA window.

jon: Observability vendor (CloudWatch Logs) ingestion 429s mean traces/metrics delayed. We should reduce noisy logging from worker retries to avoid exacerbating the vendor throttles.

ashwin: Pushing a quick patch to reduce debug logs on retry loops (build and deploy to runtime-safe group):

```
# disable heavy retry logging
kubectl set env deploy/runtime-worker LOG_RETRY_DETAILS=false -n prod
```

maria: Done. That should ease ingestion pressure.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff: oncall changed from maria -> jon at 3167778000.

jon: Taking over. Current mitigations in place: routing prefer-region us-west-2, dedicated pool drain in us-east-1, token cache TTL increase, reduced logging. Monitoring error rate.

kevin: Noticed a subset of customers pinned to us-east-1 (regional affinity). I'm running a migration for pinned customers where possible; for some regulated tenants we can't move—will open escalation to sales/CS to contact those customers.

maria: Customer-impact assessment: approx 6% of requests still failing (mostly pinned tenants and long-lived sessions), latency for others reduced to ~400-600ms p95 after routing change. Hosted API overall error rate dropped from 12% -> 3.5% in last 10m. Dedicated pools errors down from 9% -> 2.2% where rerouted.

tara: Sending proactive message to impacted customers now. Template: short explain + mitigations + ETA for next update in 30 minutes.

jon: Engineering actions next: 1) continue routing preference and monitor for AWS status resolution; 2) prepare rollback plan for config if any regressions; 3) escalate to AWS account team for STS/CloudWatch follow-up with logs and NAT flow captures; 4) create incident ticket for postmortem.

maria: I'm collecting NAT capture and STS error traces and attaching to incident ticket.

ashwin: Quick note: some internal eval jobs were auto-retry storms causing extra load — paused noncritical batch jobs.

kevin: Dedicated ops: scaling up us-west-2 standby capacity by 20% to absorb traffic.

jon: Monitoring: dashboard link https://dashboards.redwood/incidents/3167777777. If error rate goes below 1% and AWS marks region recovered, we'll start gradual rollback and un-drain us-east-1 nodes.

maria: TL;DR: cause = AWS regional STS + CW ingestion degradation. Mitigations = prefer-region routing to us-west-2, token cache TTL bump, reduced logging, drain and migrate dedicated pools, pause noisy jobs. Customer comms in progress.

tara: CS: will send final update in 30m.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert suppression applied for the next 15m to reduce noise while mitigations propagate.

jon: If anyone sees a regression after config rollouts, ping me directly. I'll own cleanup and postmortem.

maria: Adding runbook notes: add explicit step to increase token_cache_ttl during STS regional outages; add a routing quick-action to prefer alternate regions.

kevin: Opening postmortem ticket INC-3167779 and assigning owners.

tara: Thanks all — good coordination. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned to SRE rotation.

jon: I'll update channel when we start rollback or AWS reports full recovery. End of thread for now.
